newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian banks loan growth slows - Bank Negara.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian banks loan growth slows - Bank Negara.

text.p: Malaysian banks' loan growth slowed in the first half of 1996 to 11.7 percent against 15.7 percent in the preceding six-months and 12.4 percent in the corresponding period of last year, Bank Negara said on Tuesday.
The central bank said the Malaysian commercial banks' total deposits grew by 8.5 percent in the first six months against 10.3 percent in the same period of last year.

Bank Negara said the banking industry's total assets rose by 27.4 billion ringgit or 9.4 percent to 319.6 billion ringgit by the end of June, 1996. This compares with a 9.7 percent growth in the corresponding period of last year.
The central bank said in a statement issued after its 38th annual meeting with chief executives of commercial banks that two-thirds of the deposit growth came from fixed deposits.
The largest share of loans at 30.4 percent was to the property sector, followed by finance, insurance and business services sector at 19 percent.
The central bank said non-performing loans of the industry declined to 4.2 percent of total loans at the end of June 1996 from 6.1 percent at the end of June 1995.
It also told the conference of a proposed changes to the "method for valuing credit exposure for derivatives" for banks' reporting requirements.
"The refinement was made on account of the need to improve the standard of assessing risks in this new and potentially growing area of business," the Bank Negara statement said.
